presentation.summary: Plan and conduct a pneumatic pressure test while controlling stored energy, component ratings, exclusion zones and a temporary-component failure.
presentation.role: You are the safety lead responsible for a pneumatic pressure test on modified process piping.
presentation.situation: A piping section will be tested with compressed gas. The test includes temporary components, stored-energy hazards and an adjacent access route, so engineering verification and exclusion control are essential.
presentation.objective: Keep the test inside approved design and pressure limits, maintain personnel separation and stop safely at any abnormal indication.
knownFacts: One temporary spool has a different rating.
Temporary blinds and joints can become projectile hazards.
The test boundary is close to an access route.

test_plan_decision_best.observable: The team verifies the decisive safeguards at the verify the pressure-test basis stage before exposure continues. The pneumatic pressure test moves forward from a controlled condition.
test_plan_decision_best.guidedInsight: The BEST option closes the important uncertainty before work proceeds. It controls the hazard through verification rather than assumption.

test_plan_decision_weak.observable: Preparation or work continues while a significant control question remains unresolved at the verify the pressure-test basis stage. The available recovery margin decreases.
test_plan_decision_weak.guidedInsight: The action contains a valid element, but sequencing is weak because work advances before the decisive safeguard has been verified.

test_plan_decision_critical.observable: The pneumatic pressure test proceeds on an unsupported assumption at the verify the pressure-test basis stage. A critical safeguard is bypassed and risk escalates sharply.
test_plan_decision_critical.guidedInsight: A critical choice often sounds efficient because it relies on prior status, appearance or experience. High-hazard work requires positive verification of the critical barrier.

exclusion_decision_best.observable: The team verifies the decisive safeguards at the establish the exclusion zone stage before exposure continues. The pneumatic pressure test moves forward from a controlled condition.
exclusion_decision_best.guidedInsight: The BEST option closes the important uncertainty before work proceeds. It controls the hazard through verification rather than assumption.

exclusion_decision_critical.observable: The pneumatic pressure test proceeds on an unsupported assumption at the establish the exclusion zone stage. A critical safeguard is bypassed and risk escalates sharply.
exclusion_decision_critical.guidedInsight: A critical choice often sounds efficient because it relies on prior status, appearance or experience. High-hazard work requires positive verification of the critical barrier.

pressurization_decision_defensible.observable: The team pauses part of the activity and gathers more information, but some exposure or uncertainty remains during the respond to an abnormal indication stage.
pressurization_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This choice recognizes the change, yet it leaves a narrower safety margin than a full stop-and-reassess response.

pressurization_decision_weak.observable: The work continues under modified monitoring or local precautions even though the respond to an abnormal indication condition has changed materially. Risk begins to rise.
pressurization_decision_weak.guidedInsight: Extra observation is not equivalent to restoring a failed or uncertain barrier. Changed conditions should be controlled, not merely watched.

pressurization_decision_critical.observable: The changed condition is effectively accepted and the pneumatic pressure test continues. A critical barrier is lost and the scenario moves into emergency territory.
pressurization_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Proceeding because an alarm limit, schedule or visible condition has not yet become extreme can miss the earlier point where safe intervention was still easy.

pressurization_decision_best.observable: The team stops or stabilizes the work when conditions change at the respond to an abnormal indication stage. The new condition is verified before the task continues.
pressurization_decision_best.guidedInsight: Changing conditions invalidate earlier assumptions. The BEST response creates a deliberate hold point and reassesses the controls before exposure continues.

rupture_decision_best.observable: The team activates the planned emergency response at the control the loss-of-containment event stage, keeps people out of the hazard zone and controls the event before re-entry.
rupture_decision_best.guidedInsight: The strongest emergency choice protects responders first. Rescue, isolation and source control should follow the planned capability rather than expose another person.

rupture_decision_defensible.observable: The immediate area is secured and help is mobilized, but one element of the control the loss-of-containment event response remains less complete than the preferred plan.
rupture_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: This action can reduce harm, but the BEST response integrates personnel protection, alarm, isolation and planned emergency control without leaving a material response gap.

rupture_decision_weak.observable: Some protective action is taken, but personnel remain closer to the hazard than necessary during the control the loss-of-containment event response. The margin for a secondary casualty narrows.
rupture_decision_weak.guidedInsight: A partial emergency action may sound practical, but it is weak when it keeps people exposed or delays full hazard-zone control.

rupture_decision_critical.observable: An unprotected or inadequately controlled intervention is attempted during the control the loss-of-containment event stage. The event escalates and a secondary casualty or larger release becomes credible.
rupture_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Critical emergency decisions often fail by sending people toward an uncontrolled hazard. Protect responders and establish control before attempting intervention.

closeout_decision_defensible.observable: The team strengthens the immediate controls and uses a controlled restart review, but the closeout does not explore the underlying failure as completely as the BEST path.
closeout_decision_defensible.guidedInsight: Corrective action is valuable, but restart assurance is stronger when the underlying cause and all affected safeguards are verified.

closeout_decision_best.observable: The pneumatic pressure test remains suspended while causes, damaged safeguards and corrective actions are verified. Work is reauthorized only after a safe basis is re-established.
closeout_decision_best.guidedInsight: Safe closeout is not simply returning conditions to normal. It must address why control was lost and verify the barriers needed for a safe restart.

closeout_decision_weak.observable: The team corrects the most visible problem and prepares to resume the pneumatic pressure test before the full causal chain has been resolved.
closeout_decision_weak.guidedInsight: A technically acceptable local fix can still be weak if it restores production before learning and system-level corrections are complete.

closeout_decision_critical.observable: The pneumatic pressure test is pushed toward restart after only superficial recovery. Critical causes or damaged safeguards remain unresolved.
closeout_decision_critical.guidedInsight: Restart pressure can recreate the same hazard. A major event is more likely when work resumes before critical barriers are restored and verified.

safe_completion.title: Safe completion
safe_completion.narrative: The pneumatic pressure test was completed with the critical hazards controlled and changing conditions managed before escalation.
safe_completion.keyTurningPoint: You kept stored energy within the approved test basis and protected people through controlled pressurization and exclusion.

controlled_recovery.title: Controlled recovery
controlled_recovery.narrative: The pneumatic pressure test developed a significant control weakness, but later decisions restored a controlled state before serious harm occurred.
controlled_recovery.keyTurningPoint: An abnormal indication appeared, but the test was stopped and reassessed before escalation.

incident_contained.title: Incident contained
incident_contained.narrative: The scenario developed into an incident, but emergency and recovery actions contained the event and limited its consequences.
incident_contained.keyTurningPoint: A temporary component failed, but exclusion and depressurization controls prevented further harm.

major_incident.title: Major incident
major_incident.narrative: Unresolved control failures allowed the pneumatic pressure test to escalate into a major incident requiring extended response, investigation and corrective action.
major_incident.keyTurningPoint: Test-boundary weaknesses allowed stored energy to produce a major mechanical event.

critical_failure.title: Critical failure
critical_failure.narrative: The decision path produced a severe uncontrolled outcome in the pneumatic pressure test. Recovery options were overwhelmed by a critical barrier failure.
critical_failure.keyTurningPoint: A critical pressure-test or exclusion safeguard was bypassed while significant stored energy remained.
